key_insight: Later-generation OpenAI configurations showed higher emergency sensitivity, but no system performed best across all urgency categories.
clinical_relevance: Self-triage evaluation should assess emergency recognition separately from overall agreement, because high agreement can coexist with missed emergencies.
method: Compared study-specific SmED and Infermedica implementations with five structured OpenAI configurations.
Used an LLM-based patient actor across 480 physician-curated vignettes derived from German routine triage data.
Compared three-category urgency recommendations with preliminary physician consensus using frequency-based weights.
evidence_signal: Weighted emergency sensitivity ranged from 51.3% to 99.9%, while exact three-category agreement ranged from 54.4% to 68.8%; gpt-4.1 had the highest agreement but lowest emergency sensitivity.
watch_item: This vignette-based, cross-sectional comparison used preliminary expert consensus and did not directly evaluate the manufacturers’ certified triage products or establish longitudinal accuracy improvement.
paper_title: Benchmark Self-Triage (BeST): Comparing Self-Triage Systems and Multiple Generations of OpenAI Models Against Preliminary Expert Consensus
